interface.title: Jdaviz (opened from the Imviz launcher tile), Solara web app
interface.field: Astronomy: JWST/HST imaging, spectroscopy and IFU cubes
interface.stage_of_work: Quick-look inspection and first measurements on reduced data
interface.what_it_is_for: Load astronomical FITS images (or spectra and cubes) into linked viewers, align exposures on the sky, adjust how they are displayed, mark regions and measure sources with aperture photometry. This record covers the imaging side only; spectra and cubes were not reached.

data.note: The suggested folder /work/prep/data (and prep/seed) was empty on the server, and the 'file drop' source is a drop zone with no file input, so the browser could not upload into it. I found the same test files with the server's own file browser at /work/app/jdaviz/configs/imviz/tests/data (ds9_annulus_01.reg, gauss100_fits_wcs.fits, gauss100_fits_wcs_block_reduced.fits, gauss100_fits_wcs_block_reduced_rotated.fits, miri_i2d_lonlat_gwcs.asdf). I loaded gauss100_fits_wcs.fits as layer A and the rotated block-reduced file as layer B. Deployment issue, not part of the workflow: the server file browser is not limited to the app folder; while searching it let me into the host's root and /usr/lib.

tree.general: Inspect two exposures of the same field, compare them, and measure a source (images only)
tree.specific: Imaging quick-look in Jdaviz opened from the Imviz tile: load FITS images, link by WCS, blink, restyle, and run aperture photometry on a drawn aperture. Spectra (Specviz/Specviz2D) and cubes (Cubeviz) are not covered

features.name: Format-sniffing importer with alignment options
features.general: Browse server folders, pick a file, have the tool detect its type, review import options including how to align it with data already shown, and load it into a chosen view
features.specific: Import Data sidebar (Source = file; the dropdown also lists file drop, url, astroquery, virtual observatory): Load Local File browser; Importer detects 'Image' and offers Extension, Parent Dataset, Data Label, Approximate GWCS with FITS SIP, Align by Pixels/WCS, Viewer, then IMPORT or IMPORT (OVERWRITE)
steps: double-click through folders to the file
click the file (shows 'searching for valid formats...')
review the detected format, extension and data label
choose Align by Pixels or WCS and the target viewer
serves_tasks: Add a second, offset and rotated exposure aligned on sky coordinates

features.name: Sky-aligned multi-image viewer with blink
features.general: Stack several images of one field aligned by real-world coordinates and flip between them
features.specific: Align by WCS (Sky) on import; Blink tool (click or 'b' next, right-click or 'B' previous) cycles the visible layer
steps: import the second image with Align by WCS (Sky)
click viewer or press b to cycle layers
serves_tasks: Add a second, offset and rotated exposure aligned on sky coordinates
Flip between the aligned exposures to spot differences

features.name: Live cursor readout
features.general: Show the pixel position, data value and sky coordinates under the cursor for the visible image
features.specific: Top bar readout: layer letter, Pixel x/y, Value, World RA/Dec in ICRS and degrees; follows the layer shown by Blink
steps: place the cursor or click on the image
read pixel, value and RA/Dec in the top bar
switch layers and compare RA/Dec at the same spot to confirm alignment
serves_tasks: Flip between the aligned exposures to spot differences

features.name: Layer display options with live stretch histogram
features.general: For a chosen layer, set color map, opacity, contrast/bias and an intensity-mapping function and clip range, while a histogram shows the mapping curve
features.specific: Plot Options plugin: layer tabs A/B, Show Image toggle, Colormap (Gray, Viridis, Plasma, Inferno, Magma, Purple-Blue...), Image Opacity, Contrast, Bias, Stretch Function (Linear, Square Root, Arcsinh, Logarithmic, Spline, DQ), Stretch Percentile Preset (Min/Max, 99.5, 99, 95, 90%, Custom), histogram with stretch curve and More Stretch Options
steps: choose a percentile preset and check the histogram curve
serves_tasks: Change color scale and intensity mapping of one layer

features.name: Viewer navigation toolbar
features.general: Reset, box-zoom, pan/zoom with the wheel and drag on an image canvas
features.specific: Imviz viewer toolbar: Home (reset zoom to all visible data), zoom box, Pan/Zoom (wheel zoom, drag pan), subset tools, blink, fullscreen; in the run, wheel zoom did nothing while Blink was selected (seen once, not replayed)
serves_tasks: Zoom into and move around the image

features.name: Region drawing tools
features.general: Draw a shaped region on an image that becomes a named, editable selection usable by measurement tools
features.specific: Viewer toolbar subset tools (circular ROI used); dragging creates 'Subset 1' with edit handles, a colored legend badge (C), and the top selection pill switches from 'create new' to 'Subset 1'
steps: check the new subset in the selection pill and legend
serves_tasks: Mark a region around a source

features.name: Aperture photometry with curve of growth
features.general: Pick a drawn region as the aperture with a background choice, compute, and get a growth curve plus a results table that builds into a history
features.specific: Aperture Photometry plugin: Data, Aperture (a subset; no annulus/composite), Background (Manual value or a subset), Pixel area, Counts conversion factor, Flux scaling, Plot Type Curve of Growth; CALCULATE gives xcenter/ycenter, RA/Dec center, sum, sum_aper_area, min/max/mean/median/mode/std/mad_std/var, biweight stats, fwhm, semimajor/semiminor axes, orientation, eccentricity, plus a Results History table (31 columns) with an export control that was seen but not tried
steps: choose the data and the aperture subset
set the background (manual value or subset)
read the curve of growth and the results table
serves_tasks: Measure the flux and shape of the marked source

features.name: Layer legend / data menu
features.general: List the datasets in a view, toggle each one's visibility, and set the view orientation
features.specific: Click the A/B/C legend badges at the top right of the viewer: layer rows with an info button and an eye toggle, an Orientation dropdown (Default orientation), and delete/label actions
serves_tasks: See which layers are loaded and which are shown
